opti-1: Dawn over a quiet lake. Two bald eagles ride the morning air.
opti-2: Long ago, people sprayed a bug poison called DDT almost everywhere.
opti-3: It washed into lakes and fish. Eagles ate the fish, and their eggshells grew thin.
opti-5: Then people chose to act. They banned DDT and protected eagle nests.
opti-6: Year by year, the eagles came back.
opti-7: Today, bald eagles nest in every state except Hawaii.
opti-8: So how do people protect the natural world? And why does it matter?
24-01-welcome: Our film starts at dawn with two bald eagles. First, inspect a manatee with some strange marks on its back.
24-01-lesson: Today you're a conservation scientist. Watch eagles come back, test two dunes, then climb a tree full of life.
24-01-check: Three quick questions. It's not graded. It's just for you, so give each one your best try.
24-01-assign: Time to show what you learned. Sort some real actions, then tell us how you'd protect a place you know.
how-24-01-specimen: Press Inspect specimen. Move the magnifying lens over the manatee, then tap three things you notice.
how-24-01-compare: Put the water under one tray and the fan under the other: drag them, or tap one, then a tray. Press Run the test. Then swap.
how-24-01-wall: First, make a prediction. Then brush the glowing stop: drag across it (or tap it again and again) until the place shows.
how-24-01-det: Pick three cases, one at a time. Tap a clue, then pick the problem. Predict the solution that helped, and watch the place today appear.
how-24-01-write: Think of a natural place near you. Answer the three questions. Use at least two of the science words under the boxes.
how-24-01-partc: Draw one habitat twice: damaged on the left, and helped by conservation on the right. Label what changed.
